verdict: hotel_room_r3 (mean 5.75, lowest materials and cast at 5). It is a little better than r2, but it still would not pass in a fern film. What works now: accept is a real establishing frame. The bed runs on a diagonal, the lamp makes an island, and the title area is clean (graded max about 40 against the 41-42 limit, clear of the headboard cap, whose dark band ends at about y 155 on the 1920 frame). Both overheads are clean top-down compositions with good falloff, and nothing clips anywhere (no graded pixel above Y 245). Five things still look amateur. (1) The recurring tote is mustard in accept: graded a/b hue about 68 deg at chroma about 16-17, against the lead's target of 60-65 deg at 13-14 (00:40 note). The raw tote is pure orange (front-panel median RGB about 102/50/0, a blue channel of zero). In overhead it is camel (63.5 deg, in range, but chroma 19-20). Overhead_pre is near target (about 58-63 deg, chroma 11-14 depending on the mask; it is seen mostly from above). (2) The city in window looks like cut paper. Pale grey downward-pointing zigzag shapes hang across the near blocks. They are most likely the roof faces seen from above, which building_mat lights several times brighter than the upper facades. Beige sign panels float above the roofs like cardboard cards. The window cells shrink only a little from the near blocks to the middle distance. The middle blocks keep the near blocks' contrast (graded p95 about 70-85 in both), and only the tallest far towers fade into haze, so there is little depth. (3) In pack, the glowing lamp shade runs off the right edge of the frame. Its top rim is in frame, about 24 px down. It is half in and half out, which the lead ruled out for the overheads in C32. Two pale plastic buckles on the black duffel are the highest-contrast small shapes around the action and pull the eye from the hobo. The arm is a huge featureless dark sleeve ending in pale stone hands with no finger separation (the stone finish is the design; the mitten shape is not). (4) In overhead_pre the 'bracing' hand reads as a wave. From above, the arm makes an L out to a flat hand with spread fingers. Dawn's crown shows a small dark X-shaped mark in both overheads, which reads like a mark and is close to letter-like. (5) In overhead the partly closed zip barely reads at 1280, so the 'packed' beat rests only on the hobo's absence. Technical: graded luma below 8/255 covers 21.5% of overhead, 18.5% of overhead_pre and 13.4% of accept. DECISIONS records an 8.6% average for the fixed grade over seven frames. Here the dark pixels are the room-side carpet and nightstand, so this is a lighting matter, not a grade one.
answers:
Q1, does pack clearly show the hobo entering the duffel? Mostly, but not clearly. The hobo hangs from her hand by its strap and its lower part goes dark, so you can tell it is going down into something. But the duffel's near lip does not overlap the bag. In the brightened raw crop, the hobo's base ends in a curved lower edge that hangs over the black interior with nothing in front of it. That reads like a bag held over a hole, not one sinking into a mouth. The duffel's own strap crosses in front of the bag's lower right, which helps a little. The two pale plastic buckles (one at about 240,445 and one at 680,540 on the 1280 frame, graded Y up to about 90 and 130) are the highest-contrast small shapes around the action and pull the eye away from it. Verdict: it reads as 'lowering toward the bag', not unmistakably 'into the bag'.

Q2, does the partly zipped packed overhead read as a later moment? Partly. The hobo is gone from the row, the duffel is there with its far end closed, and her right hand is at the pull. Those say 'later'. But the zip line is barely visible at 1280, and nothing tells the viewer where the hobo went. The open case is not a problem. cut.json puts this plate at 03-04 on 'Her luggage was already full' ('on the packed case from above'). The case open with folded clothes, after 03-02's closed case, reads as her having opened it to pack, not as going back in time (the two shots are not adjacent; the cabin shot sits between them). A note for the edit: 03-04 comes before the market (03-05 to 03-07) and before pack (03-08). A strong 'later than pack' read would therefore run backwards in the film. That is a question for the lead, not the stage.

Q3, do the leather and textile cases stay distinct? Yes. In overhead the tote is warm and light (L about 37-40, chroma about 19), while the open case and the duffel are near-neutral black (chroma about 2). The satchel separates from the duffel by its shape, gloss and gold clasp. In pack the out-of-focus tote at right is dark ochre (hue about 66-68, chroma about 9-10, L about 16) and the case corner is neutral black, so they are distinct there too. In pack, though, the tote reads as an anonymous tan box with studs, not as the tote.

Q4, weight on the mattress in accept: it reads, but only moderately. Around her hip there is a visible basin with a soft rim, and the duvet rises beside her thigh (the 'Dawn at the bed edge' shape key: a 6 cm basin plus an 11 mm rim). The tote hangs against her knees, not floating. Acceptable, but the dip is shallow for a seated adult at 1280. The only creases are the shape key's faint 6 mm ripples in the rim, and nothing runs out from the load.

Q5, both bracing hands in overhead_pre: the hand on the case is good, with curled fingers over the top near the handle. The other hand is not bracing. From above, her left arm makes an L: the upper arm runs toward the head of the bed, and the forearm turns in across the duvet to a flat hand at about (-1.37, -0.80) with the fingers spread apart (articulate_hand 'L' is 4-12 deg per joint). It reads as reaching or waving. A hand carrying weight sits closer in under the body, with the arm more upright so it foreshortens from above, and the fingers relaxed and curled. It should still stay clear of her shoulder's silhouette, which is why the lead moved it out in C32.

Q6, distance between the warm room and the cool city in window: there is not enough distance, in colour or in depth. Colour: the lamp shade is hue about 57, chroma 11, and the sheer is cool (b about -8 to -11). But the wall around the lamp is almost neutral (chroma about 4, L 18-30), and Dawn's head is cool (b about -6). So the warm side is only the shade itself, not a warm room. Depth: the window cells shrink only a little from the near blocks to the middle distance, the middle blocks keep the near blocks' contrast, and there is no haze step between them. Only the tallest far towers fade. The city reads as a backdrop just outside the glass, not as a view from 27 floors up across a harbour.

Builder's claims checked: the accept title rectangle measured a maximum of about 40 (99.9th percentile 35-39, mean about 20) on a 1920 upscale, and it starts just below the end of the headboard cap's dark band. The vertical channel stripes behind it run from about 11 to 38: low contrast, but busy behind the serif type. Both overhead shades are inside the frame, but overhead_pre's shade sits only about 3 px from the top edge (rows 3-6 already reach Y 97-114), so in effect it touches the edge. Overhead has about 19 px of clearance. Tote: as above, accept fails (about 68 deg, chroma 16-17), overhead is too saturated (63.5 deg, chroma 19-20), overhead_pre is near target, and pack is too yellow and dark (about 66-68 deg, chroma 9-10).

fixes.problem: The film's recurring tote reads mustard in accept: graded a/b hue about 68 deg, chroma about 16-17 (target 60-65 deg, 13-14, from the lead's 00:40 note). The raw tote is pure orange (front-panel median RGB about 102/50/0). Overhead is camel (63.5 deg, chroma 19-20). The raw hue is about the same in every camera (about 56-60 deg). The yellow comes from the grade acting on a raw colour whose blue channel is clipped to zero, not from the warm duvet bounce.
fixes.fix: In hotel_room_props.PROPS['handbag-tote'], cut sat from 1.0 to about 0.75-0.8, so the raw blue channel is no longer zero (aim for a raw front panel near RGB 110/60/30). Move hue from 0.53 toward 0.50, as the lead's 00:40 note asks ('at or just under 0.50'). Try 0.51 first: overhead_pre is already near target at 0.53 and must not turn salmon. Then measure the graded front panel in every camera with a chroma mask: a/b hue 60-65 deg and chroma 13-14 in accept AND overhead. Leave duvet_bounce at the 1.2 the lead set in C32 for the hands and face.

fixes.problem: The city looks like cut paper. Pale grey downward-pointing zigzag shapes hang across the near blocks. building_mat gives the roofs an emission of (0.018 + lip 0.038)*K, against about 0.0045*K on the upper facades, so the shapes are most likely the roof faces seen from above. Beige sign panels float above the roofs like cards. The near and middle blocks have the same contrast (graded p95 about 70-85) and no haze step between them, so there is little depth and no sense of the 27th floor.
fixes.fix: In hotel_room_city.building_mat, cut roof_light from (0.018 + lip 0.038)*K to about (0.004 + lip 0.010)*K, so the roofs go darker than the lit facades, as the code's own comment intends ('darker roof membranes'). Confirm the cause first with one test render with roof_light at 0. In rooftop_signs, drop the orange (1.0, 0.6, 0.2) entry from pal, because orange panels turn beige after the grade. Keep the signs themselves: blank lit signboards are part of the stage's design. For depth, lower FOG_BUILDINGS from 1500 to about 700. The building fog then rises from about 8% to 16% at 150 m and from about 23% to 42% at 500 m, so the middle and far blocks lift toward BUILDING_FOG while the near towers stay dark with crisp windows.

fixes.problem: The glowing lamp shade runs off the right edge of the frame. Its top rim is in frame, about 24 px down; the bright top row at x > 1080 is the wall's up-light, not the shade. Half in and half out is what the lead ruled out for the overheads in C32. Two pale plastic buckles on the black duffel are the highest-contrast small shapes around the action. The hobo's base hangs over the black interior with no lip in front of it, instead of sinking under the duffel's lip.
fixes.fix: Bring the shade wholly into frame. About 50 px of it is past the edge, so set CAMERAS['pack'] shift_x to about +0.05 (the picture moves about 64 px left), or swing the aim about 0.1 m toward +X. Check that the shade then has 15 px or more of dark beside it. Swinging the aim toward -X pushes it further out, and a 6 cm swing moves it only about 40 px, which leaves it cut. The buckles are not separate materials: the extra-bag-open prop is one Tripo mesh with one textured material. In extra_bag, add a curve or map-range after the base-colour texture that pulls values above about 0.35 down to charcoal (about 0.035), or paint the buckles dark in a copy of the texture, so the duffel stays one matte black. Lower hobo_held about 4-5 cm (grip = mouth + Vector((0, 0.015, hobo_apex.z - 0.085))) and ease the near lip 2 cm higher, so the duffel's near lip overlaps the hobo's lower fifth. Give that lip a lit zip-tape edge (duvet_bounce, or a small warm card light-linked to the lip).

fixes.problem: The 'bracing' hand reads as a wave. From above, her left arm makes an L, out toward the head of the bed and then in across the duvet, ending in a flat hand with the fingers spread (articulate_hand 'L' is nearly straight, 4-12 deg per joint). Dawn's crown shows a small dark X-shaped mark (also in overhead) that reads as a mark.
fixes.fix: In premarket_poses, bring left_target in from (-1.37, -0.80) toward her body, to about (-1.28, -0.88), so the arm stands more upright and foreshortens from above. Keep the hand clear of her shoulder's silhouette from the overhead camera: the lead moved it off the shoulder in C32, so check the render. Change articulate_hand('L') to a relaxed weight-bearing curl (f_index (14,16,6), f_middle (16,18,7), f_ring (18,20,8), f_pinky (20,22,9), thumb (12,10,6)) with the fingers closer together. For the crown, first try smoothing the hair mesh's crown, or its normals, inside the stage module for the overhead cameras only (do not edit people.py). The sculpted hair is the design, so mend the pinch rather than remove the hair. If the mark still shows, pitch the head 10-15 deg further down in both overhead beats, checking that her eyes stay on the case and on the pull.

fixes.problem: The partly closed zip barely reads at 1280, so the 'packed' beat rests only on the hobo's absence. The open case is not a fault here. cut.json uses this plate at 03-04 for 'Her luggage was already full' ('on the packed case from above'), and the open case with folded clothes carries that line.
fixes.fix: Keep the open, packed case. Do not swap in the closed case: it was placed at (-0.98, -0.52) for the pre beat and would sit inside the duffel at (-1.05, -0.63). Strengthen 'duffel zip return' (energy 9 to about 14) so the closed run of the zip shows as a thin highlight from the pull to the far end. Ask the lead before showing any of the hobo in the duffel. The plate sits at 03-04, before the market (03-05 to 03-07) and before pack (03-08), so a packed hobo there would run backwards in the film.

fixes.problem: The bed-foot runner is a large flat dark-grey slab filling the lower right foreground (x about 700-1280, y 465-720). It already uses hotel_room_mats.woven (scale 300, bump 0.56), but noise that fine does not resolve at 1280, so it reads as a slab. The room-side nightstand and the floor below it sit at graded Y 2-9 (13.4% of the frame is below 8/255).
fixes.fix: Swing the accept aim about 0.15 m toward -X. The picture moves about 60 px right and the runner shrinks toward the corner. Then re-check the title area, which was tuned on this framing: the chapter block at y 200 on 1920 must stay at max 42 or less and clear of the headboard rail. Give the runner a structure that resolves at this distance, such as a coarser woven scale (about 60-120) or a fine rib along its length, rather than more of the same fine noise. Add a weak warm area light (about 2 W, light-linked to the room-side nightstand and the floor in front of it) so that corner holds Y 10-15 instead of 2-9.

fixes.problem: Warm against cool is carried only by the shade itself (hue about 57, chroma 11). The wall by the lamp is near neutral (chroma about 4, L 18-30), so the room does not read warm against the blue city. Dawn's feet are lost at the bottom: her left leg drops behind the pale corner of the bed's foot and her right foot is cut by the frame edge. That pale corner also draws the eye.
fixes.fix: Raise TRIMS['window']['lamp_spill'] from 0.55 to about 0.9 and the wall_return energy from 15 to about 22, keeping its (1.0, 0.41, 0.17) colour. Target the graded wall around the lamp at chroma 8 or more and hue about 50, while the sheer stays cool (b about -8 to -11). Then raise the camera to z about 1.7, keeping the aim, so both shoes and their contact shadows clear the bed's corner. Do not move WIN_SPOT much toward +Y: the drape hangs at y 1.66 and the sheer at 1.74, only 0.26-0.34 m in front of her spot. Darken the corner by light-linking it out of whichever light lifts it.

fixes.problem: Graded luma below 8/255 covers 21.5% of overhead and 18.5% of overhead_pre. DECISIONS records an 8.6% average for the fixed grade over seven frames. The dark pixels are the room-side (image left) carpet and nightstand: the carpet's median Y is about 7 there, against about 15 on the window side, where the diamond pattern still reads.
fixes.fix: Add a very low cool fill light-linked only to the carpet and the room-side nightstand. Use an area light of about 1.5 x 1.5 m at z 2.4 over the room-side floor (about x -1.2, y -1.7; the head wall is at x -2.05, so keep the light inside the room), energy about 3, colour (0.55, 0.62, 0.8). The floor should hold Y 10-16 in the graded frame, so the carpet reads like the window side. Keep the bed as the clear lit island: do not lift the bed, the exposure or the grade.

fixes.problem: The lamp shade's top rim sits about 3 px from the top of the frame, which reads as touching the edge.
fixes.fix: Raise CAMERAS['overhead_pre'] shift_y from 0.045 to about 0.055 (each 0.01 moves the picture about 13 px down). Alternatively, move the camera about 0.03 m toward -X; the image top is the head of the bed, which is world -X. Either way the shade should have at least 15 px of clear dark above it, as overhead does (19 px). Check that the hobo at the bottom (y about 565-690) stays inside the frame.
